**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The licence grant in § 13 sits at the playbook's **preferred** position:

- **§ 13.1** — subscription grant runs to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," worldwide and non-exclusive, with Authorized User rights. Affiliates/contractors are named in the grant itself, so we don't even need the fallback written-notice mechanic.
- **§ 13.2** — paid-up and embedded Vendor Technology is licensed to Customer *and* its Affiliates on a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" basis, including modification, derivative works, and contractor support. § 14.3 confirms this licence reaches Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable.
- **§ 13.3** — licence rights are transferable to an Affiliate or successor via the § 24 assignment right (which allows M&A/successor assignment without Vendor consent), and Vendor may revoke or suspend only for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure period. No revocation at will.
- **§ 13.4** — restrictions are narrow, with carve-outs for legally protected reverse engineering, authorized security testing, and use of Customer Data and output.

No walk-away features are present (no "revocable" at Vendor's discretion, no exclusion of affiliates or contractors), so nothing to redline here.
